defects.title: Unsuspend blanks ispconfig_suspended_as only on the current product; another product's 'client' record comes back and Change Package copies it forward
defects.reproduction: Fresh setup: kill the old panel pid, then /opt/ispc/make-panel.sh 3 8083 and /usr/bin/php8.3 /opt/livetest/lifecycle/step09.php through step15.php, run in order. step15.log after Unsuspend: '[FAIL] 15: ispconfig_suspended_as reads blank after Unsuspend (module-effective): {"current_row":"","effective":"client"}'. After the second Change Package: 'product 1  ispconfig_suspended_as = 'client' (field 9, ... vid 17)' on an Active service. Impact: /usr/bin/php8.3 /opt/livetest/lifecycle/stale_record.php. Its log: 'after Change Package: {"current_row":"client",...}'. Then, with WHMCS status Suspended set without a module call, SuspendAccount on website-only P2 sends '#247 client_update {"locked":"y",...}' and leaves 'client: locked=y ... mail_domain active n, ftp_user n, web_database n'. The control run with the records blanked sends only 'sites_web_domain_set_status inactive' and leaves locked=n.
defects.evidence: ispconfigconnect.php:711 UnsuspendAccount calls ispconfigconnect_recordSuspension($properties, $params, null). ServiceProperties::setSuspendedAs() saves through the model, which reaches only the CURRENT product's custom-field row. The fallback reader (ispconfigconnect.php:1977-1997) reads the current product's row first. If that row is blank it takes the NEWEST value row of any product (orderByDesc id ->value()), here P3's vid 51 'client'. ChangePackage then calls $properties->resaveAll() (ispconfigconnect.php:1002), which re-saves every non-null key, including KEY_SUSPENDED_AS, into the new product.
defects.analysis: This is a module defect. It is reachable through the plan's own step 11→15 sequence: suspend on product A, set the product to B while suspended (Change Package is refused on a locked client, so the product is only saved), Unsuspend on B. currentSuspensionRecord() ignores the record while WHMCS shows Active, so everyday Suspend/Unsuspend still works. It is still wrong in three ways. (1) Admins see ispconfig_suspended_as='client' on an Active service, contradicting INSTALL.md ('Unsuspend reverses that mode and blanks the record'). (2) resaveAll copies the stale record onto every later product. (3) Whenever WHMCS shows Suspended without the module having written a fresh record (a status set by hand, as plan step 17.4 does, or upgrade check 9's 'press Suspend again'), the stale 'client' forces a whole-client lock on a website-only product. That takes mail, FTP and DB down, which website-only mode exists to prevent. The harness mirrors WHMCS Service\Properties (fields per current product, update-or-insert value rows), and the module's own comments say this is live-verified.
defects.suggested_fix: Make ispconfig_suspended_as a single per-service fact. setSuspendedAs() (and clear()) should write the value to every existing ispconfig_suspended_as value row of the service on every product, the way fallbackClearer does, as well as through the model. Exclude KEY_SUSPENDED_AS from resaveAll(), or copy it only while the service is Suspended. Add a module test covering: suspend on A, move to B, unsuspend, then change package.

defects.title: A real suspension record is hidden by a newer blank row on the product the suspended service moves to, so Unsuspend wrongly refuses
defects.reproduction: /usr/bin/php8.3 /opt/livetest/lifecycle/hidden_record.php (after the step scripts). Output: 'product 1  ispconfig_suspended_as = 'client' (vid 85)', 'product 2  ispconfig_suspended_as = '' (vid 94)'. After the product is set to P2: 'suspended_as as the module reads it now: {"current_row":"","effective":null}'. Then 'UnsuspendAccount(#5) => Unsuspend refused: this service's ISPConfig client #5 is locked, but this product suspends the website only and the module has no record of locking it - the lock comes from a whole-client suspension by an earlier build, or was set by hand in ISPConfig. ...' and '[FAIL] hidden: ... locked=y, WHMCS status Suspended'. extras.php E2 shows the same on S1.
defects.evidence: This has the same root cause as MOD-1 (fallback reader at ispconfigconnect.php:1977-1997). The current product's row exists but is blank. The any-product pass then returns only the value of the newest row, which is that same blank row, so the older real 'client' row (vid 85) is never considered. The lifecycle that produces it is ordinary: created on P1, suspended and unsuspended on P1, downgraded to P2, suspended and unsuspended on P2, upgraded to P1, suspended on P1, then moved to P2 while suspended.
defects.analysis: This is a module defect. INSTALL.md promises that 'moving a suspended service to another product no longer strands it: a client locked under the old setting is unlocked'. Here the service is stranded instead. WHMCS's automatic unsuspend on payment would fail, and the paying customer's web, mail, FTP and DB stay off until an admin applies the refusal's workaround (tick the box, Unsuspend, untick; this was verified to work). The refusal text also blames 'an earlier build' or 'a hand lock', which misdirects the operator. The failure is safe, since nothing on the panel changes.
defects.suggested_fix: Apply the same fix as MOD-1: write the suspension record to every product row of the service, so a blank row can never be newer than the real record. Or, for KEY_SUSPENDED_AS, have the reader return any non-blank value when the service is Suspended, and prefer 'client' when rows disagree. Add a module test for this row ordering.

defects.title: Step 16b(c): when the admin removes the hand lock, ISPConfig takes the website offline again while WHMCS shows Active; neither the plan nor INSTALL says so
defects.reproduction: /usr/bin/php8.3 /opt/livetest/lifecycle/step16b.php. Output: 'prev_active taken by the hand lock: {"web_domain":{"3":{"active":"n"}}}'. 'UnsuspendAccount(#3) => success' with only sites_web_domain_set_status active, and web_domain active=y while locked=y. Then '[by hand in ISPConfig] client #3 locked: y -> n' gives 'web_domain: {"domain_id":"3",...,"active":"n"}' and '[FAIL] 16b-c-final ... ["n"]' (WHMCS status Active).
defects.evidence: ISPConfig's func_client_lock('y') snapshots already-inactive objects in tmp_data.prev_active. At the hand lock, that includes the website the module had suspended website-only. func_client_lock('n') on the hand unlock restores that snapshot and sets the website inactive, even though the module's Unsuspend set it active in between. panel_admin.php reproduces client_edit.php's onAfterUpdate (datalogUpdate of locked, then func_client_lock).
defects.analysis: The module does what the plan specifies: success, hand lock left alone, no client_update. But following the plan's own cleanup ('then untick Locked in ISPConfig') leaves a customer's site offline while billing shows it Active, and nothing tells the operator. INSTALL.md only says 'A client lock you set by hand ... is left alone'. This is a plan/doc gap; the module could also reduce it.
defects.suggested_fix: Add to the step 16b(c) expected result and INSTALL.md: after removing a hand lock that was set during a website-only suspension, the website comes back inactive; press Suspend then Unsuspend (or activate it by hand). Module option: when website-only Unsuspend finds the client locked, log a decision line saying the site will return to inactive when the lock is lifted. Or refuse with 'remove the hand lock first, then Unsuspend', which is the order that works.

defects.evidence: ISPC-NEGATIVE with a wrong password: meta = {ispconfig_status:'unavailable', ispconfig_error:'panel version: The login failed. Username or password wrong.; remaining probes skipped - every retry would repeat the same failed login and extend the panel lockout window', sso_state:'unknown'}. The rendered block lines are 'Single Sign-On: Cannot tell - grant get_function_list to this server's remote user' and 'Probe Errors: ...'. On the 302 host the error is 'panel version: HTTP status 302 from http://127.0.0.2:80/remote/json.php?login; remaining probes skipped - every retry would repeat the same failed login ...' with the same SSO line. Source: ispconfigconnect.php:1796 writes sso_state=STATUS_UNKNOWN when gather() aborted on a connection-level failure. hooks/ispconfigconnect.php:349 maps 'unknown' to 'Cannot tell - grant get_function_list to this server's remote user'. lib/Server/RemoteMetaData.php:203 always says 'failed login'.
defects.analysis: Module defect in the diagnostic text; the logic is fine: one request, no second login, never throws, all verified. 'unknown' is overloaded. It means both 'the get_function_list probe was refused' (the advice is right) and 'we never got a session' (the advice is wrong). An admin with a bad password, a wrong port or a proxy redirect is told to change a grant that is already there. live:connection.harness_notes:
Where everything lives: all scripts, logs and evidence are in /opt/livetest/connection/. run-all.sh runs everything: setup, steps 4-8, then meta-render. It starts and stops the fake servers under srv/ itself. The main logs are run-php83-*.log and run-php82-*.log; the per-run JSON evidence is evidence-<script>-<tag>.json.

Results:
- PHP 8.3: 189 assertions, 184 PASS. 5 FAIL:
  - 2 are D1 (the Server-group expectation in the plan).
  - 3 are D2 (my own extra check on the SSO line).
- PHP 8.2 (repo readiness runtime): identical results. That runtime ships mysqlnd, pdo_mysql and mysqli but does not enable them. /opt/livetest/connection/php82.sh loads them with -d extension=...
- Zero PHP warnings, notices, deprecations or fatals. The 8.2 runtime ran with error_reporting=-1.
- /opt/ispc/p2/php-error.log stayed empty.
- The redirect catcher was never hit.

Harness fidelity:
- Using harness.php is faithful for this slice. logModuleCall masking behaves like WHMCS replaceVars, and the Capsule-backed tables are real.
- I did not edit harness.php. My extensions are in common.php:
  - panel request-log counters;
  - attempts_login access;
  - grant setting in the exact CHECKBOXARRAY format (group keys joined with ';', per admin/form/remote_user.tform.php);
  - lt_store_remote_meta(), which mimics WHMCS storing GetRemoteMetaData output as JSON in tblservers_remote.
- Setup: ISPC-TEST and ISPC-NEGATIVE both point at 127.0.0.1:8082 with Secure off. The panel is plain-HTTP php -S, so TLS and port 8080 are not exercised.
- ISPC-NEGATIVE uses a throwaway remote user 'negative' (nine groups) and has no products.
- For step 6 I used the nine documented groups. make-panel's default user ticks every group, including Roundcube and acme-proxy, which overlap with the module's grants.

Harness gaps and differences from real WHMCS:
1. Test Connection hostname path (see D4). In WHMCS the Test Connection button builds params from the form through WHMCS\Filter\HostAddress. harness_server_params() reads the raw tblservers row, which matches only the stored-record paths (getServerParams(model): Servers refresh, service calls).
2. Param types. WHMCS passes serversecure as a bool and adds server/serverhttpprefix. The harness passes ''/'on'. Harmless: Params::serverConfig tests !== ''.
3. The Servers page itself can't run here. 'Loading the Servers page' was simulated by calling GetRemoteMetaData per server, storing the JSON, and rendering hooks/ispconfigconnect.php's AdminAreaFooterOutput with the real Capsule. WHMCS's own page and its AJAX refresh can't run here.

Fake servers:
- php -S suppresses its access-log line when a router script is used, so the routers write their own srv/*-access.log.
- The fake servers bind 127.0.0.2:80 (redirect), 127.0.0.3:80 (HTML), 127.0.0.4:8099 (catcher) and 127.0.0.5:80 (outage proxy). Loopback is in no_proxy, so no proxy was involved.

State left behind:
- Panel 2 is still running (pid in /opt/ispc/p2/server.pid).
- remote_user 'whmcs' holds the nine groups; 'negative' is present.
- attempts_login is empty.
- remote_session has 6 rows, all accounted for: 1 from my manual curl, 5 from the deliberate mid-sweep outage runs (the session is forgotten by design on a transport failure and expires server-side).
- whmcs2 holds the last run's data.
- The fake servers are stopped.

defects.title: Duplicate ispconfig_* value rows: the property reader and the shared-client guard/usage sweep read different rows
defects.reproduction: /opt/livetest/sharing/dup-rows.php. Run: cd /opt/livetest/sharing && HARNESS_DB=whmcs4 PANEL_PORT=8084 PANEL_DB=dbispconfig4 /usr/bin/php8.3 dup-rows.php (output in dup-rows.log). Excerpt: 'D2 rows v#60 ispconfig_client_id='4', v#61 ''' -> 'D2: reader=4 | guard (from service #7, client #4) sees #8 as sharer: no | sweep clientId=0'; 'Change Password D1 -> success'; 'D2 admin tab says: Linked to ISPConfig client #4.' DUP-C: reader=4 sweep=999. DUP-D-first: 'A: reader=5 | guard ... sees #14 as sharer: no | sweep clientId=0', then 'Link B to the SAME account "dupfive11": success'.
defects.evidence: The reader in ispconfigconnect_serviceProperties() asks $model->serviceProperties->get() first. WHMCS/harness return the first row in index order, the OLDEST. The module's newest-row fallback runs only when that is blank. ispconfigconnect_effectivePropertyValues(), used by otherServicesLinkedToClient() and serverServiceRows(), keeps the NEWEST row per service even when it is blank ('$current[$id] ??= $value' stores ''), then falls to '$any', which is the same newest row. The clearer is correct: it blanks every row (DUP-CLR). tblcustomfieldsvalues has no unique key on (fieldid, relid) in real WHMCS.
defects.analysis: Module defect. Whenever an older row holds a value and a newer row is blank or different, the module operates on one client while the guard and sweep think the service is unlinked or linked elsewhere. Another service can then Link, lock, re-template or TERMINATE that client with no shared-client refusal, and the sweep bills the wrong or no client. Reachability: the plan's own step 17.3 INSERT always creates a duplicate on a real WHMCS, because the admin save already wrote a blank row. That shape (older blank, newer value) is consistent, but under first-row-only save semantics (Eloquent firstOrNew) any later setClientId (Link/Replace/adoption) writes only the older row, giving [value, ''], the broken shape (DUP-D-first). The harness's HarnessServiceProperties::save() updates ALL matching rows, which masks this (DUP-D-harness is consistent). Which semantics real WHMCS Service\Properties uses for save() and get() is unverified.
defects.suggested_fix: 1) Use one duplicate-robust rule everywhere. In effectivePropertyValues and the fallback reader, take the newest NON-BLANK row of the current product, then the newest non-blank row of any product. Make the guard conservative: a candidate is a sharer if ANY non-blank current-product row, or any non-blank row when the current product has none, equals the client id. 2) Do not trust $model->serviceProperties->get() alone. Read through the module's own query, or fail closed when get() disagrees with the newest non-blank row. 3) After every property save, normalise duplicates the way the clearer already does, e.g. UPDATE tblcustomfieldsvalues SET value=? WHERE relid=? AND fieldid IN (fields named <key>). 4) Plan: add an upgrade check that lists ispconfig_% (fieldid, relid) pairs with COUNT(*)>1, make step 17.3 an UPDATE-or-INSERT, and verify on real WHMCS which duplicate row Service\Properties get() and save() touch.

defects.title: A client held by an ISPConfig product ADDON is invisible to the shared-client guard
defects.reproduction: /opt/livetest/sharing/23b-addon.php, section 23b-G (23b-addon.log). Addon 502 on an unlinked parent created client #7 'addonparen17'. Product service W (svc 18) with Username addonparen17 -> LinkAccount returned 'success' (log #276 {"linked":true,"ispconfig_client_id":7}). SuspendAccount W -> 'success' with client_update {"locked":"y"} on client 7 (log #280); client #7 locked=y. Check '23b-G-link' FAILED.
defects.evidence: ispconfigconnect_otherServicesLinkedToClient() filters tblcustomfields.type='product' and joins tblhosting, so type='addon' rows (the addon's own ids, stored via its addon-scoped model) are never candidates. The reverse direction is guarded: an addon's Link to a client that product service S2 holds is refused.
defects.analysis: Module defect. The module explicitly supports an addon on an unlinked parent 'with its own ids'. Once that exists, any product service can be linked (by typo or wrong ticket, exactly what the guard is for) to the addon's client. That service's Suspend, Change Password, Change Package and Terminate then act on the addon customer's hosting, and client_delete_everything deletes it with no refusal. Needs a deliberate addon setup plus a wrong Link, hence medium.
defects.suggested_fix: Include addon-held links in the guard. Query type IN ('product','addon'); for 'addon' rows join tblhostingaddons on relid to get the status and apply the same Terminated/Cancelled/Fraud exclusion, and describe them as 'addon #<id> of service #<parent>'. Alternatively, refuse Link/whole-client operations when any non-blank addon row holds the client id. The addon's own guard calls must exclude only the addon's own row, not the parent service id.

defects.title: Non-canonical numeric client ids (' 4', '04', '4.0', '+4', '4e0') are read as linked but evade the shared-client guard
defects.reproduction: /opt/livetest/sharing/extras.php section X1 (extras.log): "stored ' 4' -> reader client_id=4 | guard (from D1, client #4) sees D2: no". The same holds for '04', '4.0', '+4' and '4e0'. '4' and '4 ' are seen.
defects.evidence: ServiceProperties::intValue() accepts any is_numeric() string and casts it with (int). otherServicesLinkedToClient() pre-filters with SQL tblcustomfieldsvalues.value = '4', an exact string compare in which only a trailing space is ignored (PAD SPACE), and effectivePropertyValues compares trim()'d strings with ===.
defects.analysis: Module defect, low: needs a hand-edited or imported value, but then the service operates on client #4 while other services' Terminate/Link cannot see it.
defects.suggested_fix: Make the reader strict: accept only ctype_digit(trim(value)) and treat anything else as corrupt (fail closed, as the non-positive-id path does). Or canonicalise in the guard: fetch all non-blank rows of the field and compare (int) values in PHP instead of the SQL string equality.

defects.title: Stale link: only Terminate detects it; Suspend and Change Package return raw panel validator keys, and Unsuspend reports success on a non-existent client

/opt/livetest/sharing/23-terminate.php section '23b-DB extras' (23-terminate.log). With client #6 deleted from the DB, SuspendAccount T1 returned 'Suspend failed: contact_error_empty
username_error_empty
language_error_empty
email_error_isemail
email_error_empty
' (client_update was sent for client 6, log #230). ChangePackage returned the same keys. ChangePassword returned 'There is no user account for this client_id'. UnsuspendAccount returned 'success' (client_get null, sites_web_domain_get, logout).
defects.evidence: Recipe::clientRecord() turns a null client_get into [] and carries on: suspend() then client_update()s a missing client, and unsuspend() reads 'not locked', returns false and succeeds. Only TerminateAccount calls ispconfigconnect_clientExists() and returns staleRefusal(). Nothing was changed on the panel in any case.
defects.analysis: Module defect, low. Safe, but the admin gets panel validator keys instead of 'the stored ISPConfig client id #6 no longer exists', and an Unsuspend of a service whose client is gone turns WHMCS Active with a 'success'.
defects.suggested_fix: In Suspend, Unsuspend, Change Package and Change Password (entire-client paths), treat an empty client_get record as stale and return ispconfigconnect_staleRefusal(<Operation>, $clientId) before any client_update. Recipe::clientRecord() could throw a StaleClient exception that the entry file maps to that text.

defects.title: A second ISPConfig addon on the same parent fails with a raw 'username_error_unique'; addon clients are noted as the parent's

defects.title: An addon provisioned on an unlinked parent cannot be terminated once the parent is linked later (orphaned client)
defects.reproduction: /opt/livetest/sharing/extras.php section X4 (extras.log): addon 601 Create -> success (client #8); parent U2 Link to dupfive11 -> success; addon 601 Terminate -> 'Terminate failed: ISPConfig Connect cannot run on this product addon: its parent service #20 is itself linked to ISPConfig client #5 ...'. Client #8 still exists. After Unlink of the parent, the addon Terminate succeeds.
defects.evidence: ispconfigconnect_serviceProperties() refuses every addon operation when the parent is linked, even though the addon's own properties are addon-scoped and its stored client id (#8) differs from the parent's (#5).
defects.analysis: Module defect, low. The blanket refusal is conservative, but it strands a live, billable ISPConfig client with no module route to remove it, and the message ('Provision this hosting as its own product service instead') does not cover an addon that already has a client.
defects.suggested_fix: When the addon already stores its own client id, allow Terminate/Suspend/Unsuspend on that id: no parent-keyed lookups run on the addon path, and the guard can exclude the addon's own row. Or at least name the addon's stored client id in the refusal so the operator can remove it.

defects.title: Plan step 17 expected texts and the forced-share INSERT
defects.reproduction: 17-sharing.log 17.1: 'Link refused: this service's ISPConfig client #1 is also linked to service #1 (Test-One.Example, WHMCS client #77, Active)...'. The plan expects '(test-one.example, ...)'. 23b-addon.log: 'Create Account failed: ISPConfig Connect cannot run on this product addon: ...'. Replace step 17.3's INSERT with UPDATE-if-exists-else-INSERT, or DELETE the service's rows for that field first, and add a clean-up step that removes the extra rows.

defects.title: Remote-API DB user create/rotation leaves database_password_sha2/postgres NULL (develop-branch panel)
defects.reproduction: 18-password.log: 'before web_database_user.database_password_sha2 = NULL' ... 'after ... = NULL'. Likewise for _postgres. database_password is rotated correctly (*82BB60... -> *AF3371...).

Setup
- Panel 4 = my instance (127.0.0.1:8084, dbispconfig4). Panel 5 = ISPC-TEST-2 (make-panel.sh 5 8085, dbispconfig5).
- To give ISPC-TEST-2 an address different from ISPC-TEST (127.0.0.1), I started an extra PHP built-in listener for panel 5 on 127.0.0.2:8085. Its pid is in /opt/livetest/sharing/p5-alt.pid (12654) and its access log is p5-alt-server.log.
- Panels 4 and 5 and the alt listener are still running.
- Every script, log and state.json is under /opt/livetest/sharing/. Run order: 00-setup, 17-sharing, 17-6-perpanel, 18-password, 18b-panel-login, dup-rows, 23-terminate, 23b-addon, extras. Env: HARNESS_DB=whmcs4 PANEL_PORT=8084 PANEL_DB=dbispconfig4, run with /usr/bin/php8.3.
- harness.php was not edited; lib.php extends it.

Where the harness may misrepresent WHMCS
- (1) HarnessServiceProperties::save() UPDATEs every (fieldid, relid) row. If real WHMCS's Service\Properties/saveSingleCustomField updates only the first row (Eloquent firstOrNew), duplicate rows behave differently. The DUP-D-first scenario shows this is exactly what exposes SH-1. HarnessServiceProperties::get() returns the first row in index order (the oldest). Real WHMCS's row choice for duplicates is unverified, and the module's reader/guard consistency depends on it.
- (2) Addons. HarnessServiceModel keys addon values by the PARENT service id (model id = serviceid) and uses addonId as the tblcustomfields relid. WHMCS keys field relid on tbladdons.id and value relid on tblhostingaddons.id. harness_params for addons also carries the parent's status and configoptions. For 23b I used my own ShAddonModel/addon_params (in lib.php) with WHMCS semantics. The harness's own addonId path gave the same refusal.
- (3) harness_add_server defaults put hostname and ipaddress both at 127.0.0.1, so any two servers built from the defaults count as the same panel for the per-panel guard. They must be overridden for multi-panel checks.
- (4) After Create the harness does not write the generated username back to tblhosting.username (the model has no save()). I set Usernames explicitly where the plan uses them.

Environment and panel
- The plan's "auth.log shows no login" can't be checked here: in this develop source, only the interface login writes auth.log, and remote API logins never do. I used tblmodulelog (no 'login' rows) plus the panel's built-in-server access log (count of POST /remote/json.php?login) as the no-login evidence.
- make-panel.sh does not install security/ids.whitelist and ids.htmlfield, so the ISPConfig interface login dies with 'Path cannot be empty' (ids.inc.php:77/100). I copied both from the source into /opt/ispc/p4/security (my instance only) to do step 18's real panel login.
- No server.sh runs, so FTP and MySQL logins can't be tested; hash-level verification was done instead.
- The repo's PHP 8.2 wrapper lacks pdo_mysql and mysqli, so nothing could be run under it.
- Refusals from the shared-client guard write no tblmodulelog row at all (only the shared-but-allowed Unsuspend logs). The plan's "record the Module Log entries it produced" is therefore empty for refusals, which is expected behaviour.

defects.reproduction: cd /opt/livetest/usage-sso-hooks && /usr/bin/php8.3 ssl-pem-probe.php  -> 'contains 2nd PEM line verbatim: YES', 'contains "BEGIN PRIVATE KEY": YES', 'print_r then str_replace -> PEM present: no', 'json_encode then str_replace -> PEM present: YES'. defects.evidence: tblmodulelog quota_get_by_user response: [{"domain_id":"1",...,"ssl_key":"-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIEugIBADANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAASCBKQwggSgAg...". RestClient::project() keeps MASKED_KEYS (ssl_key, ssl_request, id_rsa, dkim_private, relay_pass) with their RAW values in the logged copy, and passes the values as replaceVars (RestClient.php MASKED_KEYS / project() '|| self::isMaskedKey($key)'; Factory::logger).
defects.analysis: The module never reads these columns. It still hands the raw private key to logModuleCall and relies on WHMCS's str_replace over whatever text WHMCS serialises the array into. If WHMCS uses print_r (my belief, not verifiable here), the raw newlines survive and the mask matches, so production is probably safe. Any serialisation that escapes newlines (JSON, as this harness does) stores the complete key in a table every WHMCS admin can read, with debug logging on as the plan requires. The unit test (UsageLogSecretsTest) only asserts that replaceVars cover the value, not that masking works on the stored text. RestClient's own comment gives this reason for REMOVING short PII ('masking still hands the raw value to logModuleCall, so the data is only as safe as a WHMCS-side implementation detail'), and it applies even more to key material. Partly an artefact of the harness's json_encode logModuleCall; kept as a module robustness defect because the fix is local and cheap.
defects.suggested_fix: In the logged copy, replace the values of ssl_key, ssl_request, id_rsa, dkim_private and relay_pass with REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER (as PRIVATE_KEYS do) before logModuleCall. Keep the key visible (operators can still see the panel returned key material) and keep replaceVars as a second line. Add a test that serialises the logged payload with json_encode AND print_r and asserts the PEM is absent from both.

GetRemoteMetaData sets sso_state=STATUS_UNKNOWN on $abortedOnConnection.

defects.evidence: Plan 2.6: 'Where the current product's row holds a value, the old row is ignored.' That holds only while the service stays on its current product. WHMCS Service Properties returns the current product's field value, so once packageid returns to the old product, the old rows (pre-Replace client, its website/FTP/DB ids) become the service's link for every operation. INSTALL.md 'Upgrading from an earlier build' has no step for these rows.
defects.analysis: Rows are created only by the old build: its Replace/Unlink clear() touched only the current product. The new build's Replace/Unlink run the cross-product clearer, so they no longer create such rows. The new build cannot tell a stale current-product row from a live one after the move. So this is a plan/doc gap in the upgrade check designed for these rows, with an optional module safety net. Not an environment artefact: the harness models current-product scoping as the module's own docblock says was live-verified on WHMCS 9.0.6, and the deletion happened on the real panel. Likelihood is low (needs an old-build Change Package, then an old-build Replace or Unlink, then a later downgrade/upgrade back), but the consequence is irreversible deletion of the wrong ISPConfig client.
defects.suggested_fix: Plan 2.6 and INSTALL upgrade: after reviewing the 2.6 output, blank the stale copies with this SQL (validated in run-70 on real MariaDB: 28 rows, reader view unchanged for every service/key, no resurrection afterwards): UPDATE tblcustomfieldsvalues v JOIN tblcustomfields f ON f.id=v.fieldid AND f.type='product' AND f.fieldname LIKE 'ispconfig\_%' JOIN tblhosting h ON h.id=v.relid JOIN tblcustomfields fc ON fc.type='product' AND fc.relid=h.packageid AND fc.fieldname=f.fieldname JOIN tblcustomfieldsvalues vc ON vc.fieldid=fc.id AND vc.relid=h.id SET v.value='' WHERE f.relid<>h.packageid AND v.value<>'' AND (vc.value<>'' OR vc.id>v.id); Reword 2.6 to warn that old rows come back when the product changes back. Optional module net: refuse whole-client operations (at least Terminate) when a service's current-product ispconfig_client_id differs from a non-blank ispconfig_client_id on another product row. Also let the same-name Replace/Link path and ChangePackage's resaveAll blank other products' rows.

verify:MOD-1.reasoning:
I reproduced MOD-1 on my own instance: panel 109 on port 8100, WHMCS databases whmcs109 to whmcs109d. The module flaw is real, but the route the report gives, the plan's steps 11 to 15 done in the admin UI, would not produce it in real WHMCS. That result comes from how the harness models a product change. Severity is low, not medium.

How it happens: `ispconfigconnect_UnsuspendAccount` (ispconfigconnect.php:711) calls `setSuspendedAs(null)`, which saves only through the model and so writes '' to the current product's row only. `stringValue()` treats '' as "not stored" and calls the fallback reader (ispconfigconnect.php:1971-1997). Its second pass returns the newest `ispconfig_suspended_as` row on any product. If that row is another product's 'client', the module reads 'client' on an Active service. The next Change Package runs `resaveAll()` (ispconfigconnect.php:1002), which writes that 'client' onto the current product's row.

Why the plan's route does not hit it: the harness changes a product with a bare `UPDATE tblhosting.packageid`. Real WHMCS does not do that on the admin page. I checked decoded WHMCS 8.12.1 (7.4.1 matches):
- `admin/clientsservices.php:535` calls `migrateCustomFieldsBetweenProductsOrAddons($id, $packageid, $oldpid, true)` before the tblhosting update at line 626.
- `migrateCustomFields()` DELETES the service's value rows on the old product's fields, then INSERTs new rows on the new product's fields that have the same name.
- Client upgrade orders do the same (`upgradefunctions.php:708` and `:769`).

So an admin-page product change never leaves another product's row behind. With that migration re-implemented faithfully, the plan's sequence gives: 'client' moves to P1 as a new row, Unsuspend blanks it, and no stale value remains.

Where the defect is reachable in real WHMCS: product changes that skip the migration. `api/updateclientproduct.php` with `pid` only sets `packageid`, and direct DB edits or third-party tools behave the same. On that path the harness is faithful: I checked its `get`/`save` against the decoded `WHMCS\Service\Properties` and `saveSingleCustomField`. It also needs one precondition: the destination product must already hold an older `ispconfig_suspended_as` row for this service, from an earlier suspend/unsuspend there. Without that row, Unsuspend inserts a newer blank row and the fallback returns null (checked).

Impact is narrow:
- `currentSuspensionRecord()` ignores the record while the service is Active, so normal Suspend and Unsuspend, cron auto-suspend and Change Package all behave correctly.
- Real harm needs a website-only product with the stale 'client', a status set to Suspended with no module call (by hand, or by an API UpdateClientProduct status=Suspended followed by ModuleSuspend), then Suspend. That locks the whole client and takes mail, FTP and DB down. Unsuspend reverses it fully.
- Otherwise the effect is cosmetic: 'client' shown on an Active service, which contradicts INSTALL.md:407-408.

Docs defect: yes.
- INSTALL.md's claim "Unsuspend ... blanks the record" is false on the API path.
- More seriously, the module comments (ServiceProperties.php:57-63 and :223-228, ispconfigconnect.php:999-1001), the plan's upgrade check 6 and the harness all assume the old product's rows stay behind after a product change. For admin Save and upgrade orders that is wrong.

Separate finding, not MOD-1, likely more severe: the same migration deletes all of the service's ispconfig_* values when the new product has no fields with those names. After an admin Save from P1 to a fresh P3, all ids were gone and Change Package answered "Change Package refused: this service is not linked to an ISPConfig account". The fallback reader cannot recover rows WHMCS has deleted, so the plan's step 14 as written would fail on a real WHMCS whose P3 has no ispconfig_* fields yet.

verify:MOD-1.fix_notes:
Module (MOD-1):
- Treat `ispconfig_suspended_as` as one value per service. `setSuspendedAs()` should write the new value, blank included, to every `ispconfig_suspended_as` value row of the service on every product, the way `fallbackClearer` does, as well as saving through the model.
- Leave KEY_SUSPENDED_AS out of `resaveAll()`. Change Package already re-records a fresh mode when it re-suspends.
- Alternatively, for this key let the fallback reader run only when the current product has no row at all, not when its row is blank.
- Add a test for: suspend/unsuspend on B, product changed to A without migration, Change Package, suspend on A, product changed to B while suspended, Unsuspend, Change Package. The record must stay blank.

Harness (/opt/whmcs-harness/harness.php), where it misrepresents WHMCS:
- (a) It has no model of the admin-page and upgrade-order product change. WHMCS runs `migrateCustomFieldsBetweenProductsOrAddons`, which deletes the old product's value rows and inserts rows on same-named fields of the new product. The lifecycle slice's `UPDATE packageid` models only API UpdateClientProduct. A `harness_change_product_admin()` helper like the one in /opt/livetest/verify-MOD-1/lib.php would close this gap.
- (b) `HarnessServiceProperties::save` updates every matching value row. WHMCS `saveSingleCustomField` uses `firstOrNew` and updates only the first. This matters once WHMCS's insert-only migration creates duplicate rows.

Docs:
- INSTALL.md:407-408 should say the record is blanked on every product once the module is fixed.
- The module comments, IMPLEMENTATION notes and LIVE-TEST-PLAN upgrade check 6 should state the real WHMCS behaviour. The admin Save and upgrade paths move same-named values and delete the old rows. Only API, DB or third-party product changes leave old rows behind.

Separate issue for the orchestrator to triage, probably high severity: a product change through admin Save or an upgrade order, to a product that lacks the ispconfig_* field definitions, makes WHMCS delete every stored id, and the service ends up unlinked. The plan's step 14 (P1 to a fresh P3) would then return "Change Package refused: ... not linked". Possible fixes:
- Have the plan and INSTALL.md require the ispconfig_* admin-only fields on every ISPConfig Connect product before any product change.
- Or have the module create them, for example from ConfigOptions or a hook on product save.
- Or add a PreModuleChangePackage / ServiceEdit hook that re-links the service.

verify:MOD-2.reasoning:
I reproduced this on my own instance: panel 119 on port 8119, WHMCS DBs whmcs119v, whmcs119r and whmcs119p. The work is in /opt/livetest/verify-MOD-2/. It is a real module defect. It happens in fewer situations than the report says, because the harness does not model how WHMCS moves custom-field rows when a product changes.

ROOT CAUSE (module). In ispconfigconnect.php:1972-1998 the fallback reader runs `orderByDesc(tblcustomfieldsvalues.id)->value(...)` for the current product and then for any product. Each pass looks only at the single newest row and skips it if blank. So an older, non-blank 'client' record is never considered when a newer blank row exists anywhere for the service. UnsuspendAccount (lines 604-607) then gets recorded=null. On a website-only product with the client still locked, it hits the refusal at 656-667, which wrongly says the module has no record. Nothing on the panel changes, and the service stays Suspended in WHMCS.

ENVIRONMENT RULED OUT.
(a) ISPConfig / missing daemon: the refusal is decided on the WHMCS side. Recipe::clientIsLocked reads client.locked from client_get. client_update → func_client_lock writes that flag straight into the panel DB, so server.sh is not involved. Any 3.3 panel returns the same locked='y'.
(b) Harness Properties: I also re-ran every case with a model that copies the decoded WHMCS 8.12.1 Service\Properties + saveSingleCustomField. Both get() and save() use CustomFieldValue::firstOrNew with no ORDER BY, so only the first matching row is read or written. The reported sequence still fails.

SCOPE (how WHMCS changes products).
- API UpdateClientProduct(pid): the decoded 8.12.1 source only updates packageid and does not migrate custom fields. This is exactly what the harness and the reporter model. The reporter's lifecycle, with all three product changes done this way (AAA), strands the service under both the harness and the real-Properties models.
- Admin "Save Changes" (clientsservices.php:535) and upgrade orders (upgradefunctions :708/:769) both call migrateCustomFieldsBetweenProductsOrAddons → migrateCustomFields. That deletes the service's rows on the old product and INSERTs same-named rows on the new one, so the 'client' value moves to P2. With all three moves done in the admin UI (MMM), which is what LIVE-TEST-PLAN.md literally describes ("set its product..., Save Changes"), it passes. The combinations AAM, MAA, MMA, AMM and MAM also pass.
- A mixed path fails too: API, then admin Save, then API (AMA), but only under real WHMCS Properties semantics. The migrate INSERT does no upsert, so it leaves a newer blank duplicate on P1 (vid35). Real save() writes 'client' only to the oldest row (vid17). The reader then sees only vid35, which is blank. The harness save() updates every duplicate, so under the harness AMA passes.

So a real WHMCS + ISPConfig 3.3 install is stranded whenever the last move, and the move before it, bypass custom-field migration. That means API or automation-driven product changes, whether alone or mixed with admin Saves. Pure admin-UI or upgrade-order moves are not affected.

Impact is as reported: Unsuspend is refused, and so is WHMCS's automatic unsuspend on payment. The paying customer's web, mail, FTP and DB stay off until an admin applies the workaround. It fails safe, because nothing changes on the panel. The refusal text also misdiagnoses the cause ("no record", "earlier build", "set by hand").

DOCS. The claim at INSTALL.md:409-411 describes the intended behaviour correctly; it is broken by the module defect, not a separate docs error. The test plan's steps are correct WHMCS usage.

HARNESS NOTES. Two gaps:
1. Harness steps that do a plain `UPDATE tblhosting.packageid` stand for the plan's "Save Changes", but they skip WHMCS's migrateCustomFields (delete old rows, insert same-named rows).
2. HarnessServiceProperties::save() updates every duplicate (fieldid, relid) row, but real saveSingleCustomField uses firstOrNew and writes only one.

The first gap makes the plan's UI steps look worse than they are here. The second hides the AMA path.

verify:MOD-2.fix_notes:
Make the suspension record hold one value per service, whatever product and duplicate rows exist:

(1) In ServiceProperties::setSuspendedAs() (or recordSuspension()), write through the model as now. Then also update every existing tblcustomfieldsvalues row for KEY_SUSPENDED_AS of this service, across all type='product' fields and including duplicates. This is a "fallback writer" wired in ispconfigconnect_serviceProperties() the same way withFallbackClearer is. Blanking on Unsuspend must reach all of those rows too.

(2) Make the reader ignore blank rows. Add `where value != ''` in both passes, or, for KEY_SUSPENDED_AS, prefer 'client' when non-blank rows disagree. Do this only together with (1): the filter alone leaves stale 'client' rows that are then read on Active services.

(3) Change the refusal text at ispconfigconnect.php:656-667. It should not claim "no record / earlier build / by hand" as certainties; it should also mention that a record on another product may exist.

(4) Add module tests with the real WHMCS row shapes:
- a newer blank row on the destination product (API UpdateClientProduct path);
- a newer blank duplicate on the same product created by WHMCS migrateCustomFields' plain INSERT, with firstOrNew-style save writing only the oldest row.

(5) The comment at ispconfigconnect.php:970-972 ("The old product's custom-field rows do not follow the service") is wrong for admin Save Changes and upgrade orders. WHMCS migrates same-named fields there and deletes the old rows. It is right only for API UpdateClientProduct.

Harness follow-ups, for the orchestrator:
- model the plan's "Save Changes" with migrateCustomFields (see change_admin() in /opt/livetest/verify-MOD-2/lib.php);
- make HarnessServiceProperties::save() write only the firstOrNew row, not every duplicate.

verify:DOC-2.reasoning:
I reproduced DOC-2 on my own panel (N=129, port 8129, HARNESS_DB whmcs_vdoc2). I did it two ways: with the panel-code emulation, and through the real ISPConfig admin UI (login, then client_edit.php Address tab, tick or untick Locked, submitted with the CSRF token). Both give the same result.

What happens:
1. Website-only Suspend: `sites_web_domain_set_status` inactive. The client is not locked and `suspended_as` is `website`.
2. The admin ticks Locked. `func_client_lock('y')` records the already-inactive website in `client.tmp_data.prev_active` (`{"web_domain":{"1":{"active":"n"}}}`).
3. Unsuspend returns `success`. The only panel call is `sites_web_domain_set_status` active, with no `client_update`. The website is active, `locked` is still `y`, WHMCS shows Active, and `prev_active` still says the website was inactive.
4. The admin unticks Locked. `func_client_lock('n')` brings FTP, mail and the database back but sets the website to inactive (datalog `web_domain y->n`). The end state is a site that is offline while WHMCS shows Active, with nothing in any log.

This is not caused by the test environment:
- `func_client_lock` is byte-identical in the 3.3 develop tree and in a 2023 3.2-line tree (/tmp/isp-src/cyberkathosting_ispconfig3, "3.2dev"), so it is not a develop-branch quirk.
- The final state is in the master panel DB. With server.sh running, the queued datalog would simply switch the vhost off, which is the same outage.
- The real client_edit.php path gives the same result as the emulation.
- The harness only sets `domainstatus` Active when a call returns `success`, which is what WHMCS does.

It is still not a module defect:
- The module does exactly what the plan's step 16b(c) expects ("sets the website active but leaves the hand-set lock in place (no client_update)") and what INSTALL.md §6 promises ("A client lock you set by hand ... is left alone").
- The outage comes from ISPConfig's lock snapshot being restored on an admin action taken outside WHMCS, after the module call has finished.
- The module cannot fix the snapshot: `tmp_data` is not a field in any client tform or in the remote client API, so `client_update` cannot change it.
- The module could still do better: it could warn, or refuse (see fix_notes).

It is a docs defect:
- The plan tells the tester to "then untick Locked in ISPConfig" but gives no expected result for that action.
- Following the plan leaves a customer's site offline while WHMCS shows Active.
- INSTALL.md gives no warning about this.

A realistic trigger outside testing: an admin hand-locks a client (for example during an abuse investigation) while its service is website-only suspended. WHMCS then auto-unsuspends on payment, and the admin later lifts the lock.

Medium severity, because the outage is silent and hits the customer; the fix is easy once someone knows about it.

So one value means two things: "the probe was refused" and "we never got a session".

This contradicts the module's own design. Sso\SsoAdvice defines a separate STATE_UNREACHABLE ("Not checked - the panel could not be reached..."). The admin service tab and Test Connection both use it: for the same broken server, the service tab said "Not checked - the panel could not be reached" and Test Connection named the real cause (rejected login, lockout, HTTP 302, non-JSON body, curl error 7). Only the Servers page gives the wrong fix.

- **Transport cases:** the panel received 0 requests, so neither ISPConfig nor the missing server.sh daemon plays any part.

- **Harness:** it only supplies the server* params and the tblservers_remote row that WHMCS itself supplies and stores.

For 302, HTML and refused connections, Probe Errors ends with "remaining probes skipped - every retry would repeat the same failed login and extend the panel lockout window". But the panel got no request and attempts_login did not change, so no login happened and no lockout counter moved (RemoteMetaData.php:203-204 uses that sentence for every connection-level failure).

Severity is low. The Probe Errors line on the same block does carry the true reason, the client-area button logic is unaffected ('unknown' means neither offer nor withhold), and Test Connection and the service tab give correct advice.

verify:D4.reasoning:
D4 is confirmed as a defect in the plan. It is not a defect in the module, and the plan problem is bigger than the reporter said. The reporter did not have WHMCS\Filter\HostAddress. I fetched it, decoded and unmodified, from the same source their configservers.php came from: sskafandri/WHMCS-8.12.1-DECODED@2b3a936, vendor/whmcs/whmcs-foundation/lib/Filter/HostAddress.php. Their configservers.php is byte-identical to the upstream copy. I then ran the real class on panel 1310 (port 8131, WHMCS DB whmcs1310d4), wrapped in a line-by-line transcription of configservers.php action=testconnection (lines 43-86) and action=save (155-201), plus Module\Server::getServerParams and Product\Server::getHost.

What HostAddress does: it splits the input on ':', validates any port part with ctype_digit, and checks the host with FILTER_VALIDATE_DOMAIN|FILTER_FLAG_HOSTNAME. An IPv6 literal is moved to the IP field, and a port from the Hostname beats the Port field. Every Invalid* exception extends InvalidHostAddress, so the testconnection catch blocks show WHMCS's own validation.regex message. For the plan's six step-4 values, the Test Connection button therefore never shows the module's text:
- 'https://panel.test.example' becomes host 'https' with port '//panel.test.example'. InvalidPort is thrown and WHMCS shows validation.regex(fields.port). The module is never called.
- 'panel.test.example/', 'user@panel.test.example' and 'panel test.example' throw InvalidHostname and show validation.regex(fields.hostnameOrIp). The module is never called.
- 'panel.test.example:8080' is split and the module gets serverhostname=panel.test.example, serverport=8080.
- '[2001:db8::1]:8080' is split and the module gets '[2001:db8::1]':8080 when the IP field is empty. When the IP field is filled, it gets the IP Address field's value on port 8080.

In those two split cases the module is right to accept a clean host and port, and it opens a real connection and writes a tblmodulelog login row. A mapped run ('127.0.0.1:8131') returned 'Connected. Single sign-on: ...' after 16 real panel requests and 17 module-log rows. So in the plan's environment, where panel.test.example:8080 is the panel, pressing the button logs in with the throwaway user. That breaks every step-4 expectation: the refusal text, no auth.log line and no Module Log row. The reporter's suggested fix ('accept either the module text or WHMCS's own validation message') would still fail for these two values, because the button shows neither.

Save on the Servers form refuses four of the values and normalizes the other two (hostname=panel.test.example with port NULL, i.e. the 8080 default; hostname=2001:db8::1). So a malformed Hostname can only reach tblservers through SQL, the API, an import or an older build.

The reporter's other claim is right. The stored-record paths do not filter: getServerParams uses $server->getHost(), configservers.php:542 does the Servers-page refresh with the stored model, and buildParams also goes through getServerParams(serverid). With the raw value in tblservers, the module's own validation catches all six: GetRemoteMetaData and VerifyPermissions both returned the exact plan text, with zero panel requests and zero module-log rows.

None of this depends on the environment. The filter, the plan values and the module's behaviour are the same with or without server.sh and on the develop panel, and the results are identical under PHP 8.2 and 8.3 (the filter part only). One caveat: the plan targets WHMCS 9.0.x and the only decoded source I could get is 8.12.1, so 9.0 behaviour is inferred.

Separately from D4, I found a real low-severity module defect, confirmed on the stored-record path. When Hostname is empty and IP Address holds an IPv6 address written with an embedded dotted IPv4 (for example '::ffff:192.0.2.10' or NAT64 '64:ff9b::192.0.2.10'), WHMCS's Product\Server::getHost() brackets it. ServerConfig::validateHost then refuses the result with 'it is not a valid [IPv6] literal', because its bracket regex /^\[([0-9A-Fa-f:]+)\]$/ does not allow '.'. The same address written in hex ('::ffff:7f00:1') is accepted. The harness misses this because harness_server_params passes the raw, empty hostname and not WHMCS's bracketed getHost().

verify:D5.reasoning:
D5 is confirmed as a real, low-severity module defect. It is a UX gap, not a correctness problem, and there is no docs defect.

I reproduced it independently on my own panel (N=1410 on 127.0.0.1:8141, database dbispconfig1410, HARNESS_DB whmcs1410). I called Verify Permissions the way WHMCS runs a custom button: harness_call('VerifyPermissions', $serviceId), with the service's own tblservers row feeding the server fields. The live-test script instead overrode the server params of service 1.

I covered every connection-level failure the real panel can produce, not just the wrong password:
- wrong password
- IP not on the remote user's allowlist
- lockout (attempts_login.times=10)
- maintenance mode (sys_ini [misc] maintenance_mode=y)
- remote API disabled (remote_api_allowed=no)
- unreachable port

In all six cases Test Connection returns its specific remediation text. Verify Permissions returns only "Verify Permissions failed: " plus the raw panel or curl sentence. The results are identical under PHP 8.3 and the repo's PHP 8.2 runtime.

Cause in the source: ispconfigconnect_VerifyPermissions (ispconfigconnect.php:1282-1283) catches every Throwable and returns ispconfigconnect_errorString('Verify Permissions', $failure). ispconfigconnect_errorString (:2208) only prefixes the operation name to the exception message. ispconfigconnect_TestConnection (:348-351) routes the same exceptions through ispconfigconnect_connectionAdvice (:2115), as do ListAccounts, UsageUpdate, MetricProvider and singleSignOn. Verify Permissions runs the same login plus read probes as Test Connection, so it is the one diagnostic button that loses the advice.

The environment is ruled out on three counts:
- **No server.sh daemon:** irrelevant. The login and read-probe path never touches sys_datalog.
- **Develop-branch panel:** not a factor. The module classifies faults by fixed English sentences in RemoteFaultException::SENTINELS, verified against the 3.3.1p1 release. On this very panel every case mapped to the right class (LoginFailed, IpNotAllowed, Lockout, MaintenanceMode, ApiDisabled, Transport), each with isConnectionLevel()=true. Test Connection produced the correct advice from those same classes, so the difference lies only in which formatter each function's catch block calls.
- **Harness:** harness_call returns the module's string unchanged; it only updates status on 'success' for the four lifecycle functions. WHMCS shows a custom button's non-'success' return to staff verbatim, as the module's own docblock at :1232-1236 notes, citing developers.whmcs.com.

I reproduced this independently on my own instance: panel 107 on port 8177 (dbispconfig107) and WHMCS DB whmcs107sh1. Everything is in /opt/livetest/verify-SH-1/ (repro.php, lib.php, repro.log). The defect is purely WHMCS-side property logic. The panel only carried out what the module asked, so the missing server.sh daemon and the develop-branch panel play no part.

Root cause, confirmed in the source (modules/servers/ispconfigconnect/ispconfigconnect.php and lib/Support/ServiceProperties.php):
- The module reads one datum under two different rules.
- The service reader, ServiceProperties::stringValue(), asks $model->serviceProperties->get() first. It uses its own newest-row fallback only when get() returns blank.
- The shared-client guard (otherServicesLinkedToClient) and the usage sweep (serverServiceRows) both use ispconfigconnect_effectivePropertyValues(). That function takes the NEWEST row of the current product even when it is blank ($current[$id] ??= $value), then the newest row of any product.
- When duplicate (fieldid, relid) rows exist, get() and the newest-row rule return different rows, and the module disagrees with itself.

Duplicate rows are possible because the real WHMCS schema has only a non-unique KEY fieldid_relid, no unique key.

Is it a harness artefact? No, as far as I could check:
- On the same MariaDB and WHMCS indexes, every standard no-ORDER-BY read returns the OLDEST duplicate. That covers Capsule ->value() (the harness get()), Eloquent Model::where()->first(), where(relid)->get()->firstWhere() and firstOrNew(). EXPLAIN shows an index_merge intersect.
- WHMCS\CustomField\CustomFieldValue is an Eloquent model, so any usual implementation of get() reads the oldest row, as the harness does.
- The harness's save() updates ALL matching rows. That is the forgiving variant and it hides the worst case. The standard Eloquent firstOrNew() save (first row only) exposes it.
- The exact internals of WHMCS Service\Properties remain unverified. The core is ionCube-encoded, and docs.whmcs.com, developers.whmcs.com, classdocs.whmcs.com and whmcs.community are all blocked by egress.

The code also breaks the module's own documented rules, whatever WHMCS get() does:
- docs/IMPLEMENTATION-NOTES.md §5 says the sweep's rule is 'a non-empty value beats a blank … a blank never erases a live id'. The code lets a newer blank row on the current product erase an older live id. In case A the sweep returns clientId=0 for rows [M, ''].
- The guard's docblock says each candidate is 'judged by the same rule as the property reader'. That is false whenever get() does not return the newest row.

Reachability, which is why I rate it low severity:
- Neither the module nor, as far as known, normal WHMCS flows create duplicate rows. They come from hand SQL, imports or races, and from the test plan's own raw INSERTs (steps 17.3, 17.4 and 17.6).
- Followed exactly as written, the plan leaves only the consistent shape [older '', newer N], and S4 is never re-linked afterwards. So the plan does not reach the fail-open state by itself.
- Once duplicates exist, two things reach it: a hand edit, or the module's own Unlink followed by Link or Replace under first-row-only save semantics. I reproduced the second path end to end. The impact is an irreversible Terminate of another service's client with no shared-client refusal.

So this is a real but latent module defect: the shared-client safety guard fails open. Separately, the plan and docs are wrong in the ways listed in fix_notes.

Module:
1. Use one rule everywhere, and make it robust to duplicates. For each key: take the newest NON-BLANK row of the current product; if there is none, take the newest non-blank row of any product. 2. Stop trusting $model->serviceProperties->get() alone for ispconfig_* keys. Either read through the module's own ordered query first and use the model only when that query cannot run, or compare get() with the newest non-blank row and fail closed (refuse whole-client operations and name the service) when they disagree.
3. Make the guard conservative. Count a candidate as a sharer if ANY non-blank current-product row equals the client id, or any non-blank row does when the current product has none. For Terminate, it is fine to refuse when a candidate's rows disagree.
4. After every property save, normalise duplicates the way the clearer already does: UPDATE tblcustomfieldsvalues SET value=? WHERE relid=? AND fieldid IN (ids of product fields with that fieldname). Otherwise firstOrNew-style saves leave [value, ''].

Reproduced independently on my own instance: panel 117 on 127.0.0.1:8157 (dbispconfig117), WHMCS DB whmcs_vsh2, PHP 8.3. For the addon I used a WHMCS-faithful model: tbladdons and tblhostingaddons tables; addon properties stored as type='addon' custom fields on the addon definition, with values keyed by tblhostingaddons.id; serviceid = parent id; addonId = hosting-addon id; status = addon status; server* taken from the addon's server.

Root cause, from source (modules/servers/ispconfigconnect/ispconfigconnect.php:4440):
- ispconfigconnect_otherServicesLinkedToClient() only looks at rows where tblcustomfields.type='product', joined to tblhosting on relid.
- ispconfigconnect_effectivePropertyValues() (:4621) has the same restriction.
- An addon's ids live in type='addon' rows keyed by the hosting-addon id, so no addon can ever be a sharer.
- Addon use is a documented, supported configuration. INSTALL.md §4 says an addon on a parent that is not an ISPConfig service "runs on its own stored ids only". The addon branch of ispconfigconnect_serviceProperties() (:1937) implements that.
- INSTALL.md "One WHMCS service per ISPConfig client" promises that Link, Replace, Terminate, entire-client Suspend, Change Password and Change Package are refused when another live holder exists. The guard's own comment names the exact trigger: "a typo or a paste from the wrong ticket".

Environment ruled out:
- The guard is pure WHMCS-database logic. The panel is only asked to confirm the username exists.
- The panel-side effects are real ISPConfig remote code: client_update (locked, template_master), client_change_password, and client_delete_everything (remote.d/client.inc.php:391, which deletes the client, sys_user, sys_group and every row of the client's group at once). These are longstanding 3.x functions, not develop-branch specifics. The missing server.sh daemon would only additionally remove the files, mailboxes and databases on disk.
- No harness artefact: the control case (a product-held client) is refused correctly in the same environment, and the result is the same under the harness's own HarnessServiceModel addon keying (variant V2).
- Automatic adoption is not a second way in in this build (no Adopt\Resolver class ships). The only ways in are the Link and Replace buttons, which the guard exists to protect.

Also found:
- Addon to addon: a second addon on another unlinked parent can link to the first addon's client and then terminate it (variant V1).
- The guard is asymmetric. Once product service W is linked, the addon itself is refused ("also linked to service #4"). So the product side can't see the addon, but the addon side can see the product.
- The pre-upgrade audit SQL in LIVE-TEST-PLAN §2 item 5 is also product-only and did not flag the addon/product share. That is a secondary doc gap with the same root cause. The docs otherwise describe the intended behaviour correctly, so this is primarily a module defect.

Why the two sides disagree:
- The reader, ServiceProperties::intValue() at lib/Support/ServiceProperties.php:256-265, accepts any is_numeric() string and casts it with (int).
- The guard, ispconfigconnect_otherServicesLinkedToClient() at ispconfigconnect.php:4440, first filters in SQL with tblcustomfieldsvalues.value = (string)$clientId. That is an exact match, except that trailing spaces are ignored under the PAD SPACE collation.
- It then keeps a candidate only when effectivePropertyValues() returns the trimmed string and that string is === (string)$clientId.

As a result, ' 1', '01', '001', '1.0', '+1', '1e0', "\t1", "1\n" and even '1.9' all read as client #1 in B, but the guard from A does not see B. Only '1' and '1 ' are seen. The guard from B still sees A, so the gap runs one way only. The consequence is the one the guard exists to prevent:
- **Terminate:** Terminate on the canonical holder A deletes the client that B is still linked to.
- **Link:** a second service can be linked to a client that a non-canonical holder already holds.

The module's own docblock at ispconfigconnect.php:4428-4434 says every candidate is judged by the same rule as the property reader. The code breaks that stated invariant.

This is not an artefact of the environment:
1. **Missing server.sh:** the decision is made on the WHMCS side before any panel call. client_delete_everything had already removed the panel rows and queued 'd' jobs in sys_datalog, which a real server.sh would carry out.
2. **Develop-branch panel:** nothing about the panel version is involved.
3. **Harness:** the guard is raw Capsule SQL against real MariaDB with WHMCS's own column type (TEXT, utf8_unicode_ci). On MySQL 8 the result is the same with a PAD SPACE collation, and with a NO PAD collation even '1 ' would slip past the guard. The module's own fallback reader, which is module code rather than harness code, also returns raw values. Even if real WHMCS trimmed custom-field input when an admin saves it, '01', '+1', '1.0', '1e0' and '1.9' would survive the trim.

The trigger needs an admin to hand-enter or import the value in a non-canonical form. The module itself always writes (string)(int). The docs invite hand-setting in several places:
- the INSTALL.md troubleshooting row at line 880: "or its ispconfig_client_id property set";
- plan step 17.3, which inserts the value by hand with SQL;
- pre-upgrade audit step 8, which exists to catch hand-edited values.

It is also a second admin mistake stacked on sharing a client. So the chance of hitting it is low, but the impact is irreversible data loss. I rate it low.

There is also a docs defect in docs/LIVE-TEST-PLAN.md, pre-upgrade audit step 8 ("Non-positive stored ids", line 157). It says "Terminate now refuses these as stale", but for ' 1', '+1', '1.0', '1e0', '1.9' and "\t1", all of which its query lists, Terminate goes ahead and deletes the client. In addition, '01', '001' and "1\n" are not listed by step 8, and step 5 (shared clients, which groups by the raw value) does not report them as shared either. So the plan's audits miss this condition entirely.

The reporter's first suggested fix is not enough. Accepting ctype_digit(trim(value)) still lets ' 1', '01', "\t1" and "1\n" through the reader, and all four slip past the guard.

I reproduced the refusal on my own instance: panel p157 on port 8157 (dbispconfig157), WHMCS database whmcs_vsh6_157. The environment does not cause it. The refusal happens in ispconfigconnect_serviceProperties() (ispconfigconnect.php:1937-1961) before any session is opened. That function reads the parent's product custom field ispconfig_client_id through ispconfigconnect_effectivePropertyValues(), which queries tblcustomfieldsvalues. Real WHMCS stores the parent's link in that same table, so a real install would refuse the same way. Nothing here depends on the server.sh daemon, the develop-branch panel, or the harness's addon model. I got the same refusal with my own WHMCS-faithful Addon model (addon-type fields, values keyed by the tblhostingaddons id) and with the stock harness model.

Confirmed parts of the report:
- An addon provisioned while its ISPConfig-product parent is unlinked gets its own client, #1.
- After the parent is linked to a different client (#2), the module refuses every operation on the addon: Suspend, Unsuspend, Change Password, Change Package and Terminate. The addon's live client #1 stays unlocked.
- On non-payment, WHMCS therefore cannot suspend it, and on cancellation it cannot terminate it.
- The refusal text never names the addon's own client #1. It says "Provision this hosting as its own product service instead", which is useless for an addon that already holds a client.
- The design did not consider this transition. INSTALL.md and REVIEW-STATUS describe two static cases (addon on a linked parent is refused; addon on an unlinked parent runs on its own ids), not a parent that becomes linked later.

Overstated or wrong parts of the report:
1. "No module route to remove it" is false. The panel-free admin buttons work: Unlink the parent, Terminate the addon (deletes client #1), then Link the parent again (re-linked to #2, whose hosting is untouched). It is clumsy, but it works. The operator can also read the addon's ispconfig_client_id in its admin-only custom fields.
2. The suggested fix, as first worded ("when the addon already stores its own client id, allow Terminate"), is unsafe. In the most typical real sequence the parent already has a WHMCS username, the addon is created first, and the addon's client takes the parent's username (for an addon, WHMCS passes the parent's params). The parent's own Create then fails on the real panel with "username_error_unique / Duplicate username". The admin's natural next step, Link, binds the parent to the addon's client, so both hold #3. The shared-client guard is keyed on serviceid, which is the parent's id, so it excludes the parent: otherServicesLinkedToClient(parent, #3) returns []. The blanket refusal is then the only thing that stops client_delete_everything on the parent's hosting.

Any relaxation must require that the addon's stored id differs from the parent's effective id, and must still refuse otherwise. Net verdict: a real but low-severity module gap (no targeted recovery, plus a misleading message), not a safety bug. There is also a docs omission. INSTALL.md §4 does not misstate anything, but it does not warn that an addon provisioned before its parent is linked becomes unmanageable, and it gives no recovery procedure.
